<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 6:21">Targ. Jud. VI, 21</cite> (Ar. <cite ref="U00384"><he>שוטיא</he></cite>; some ed. <cite ref="U00422"><he>שולטיתא</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Ketubot 17a:6">Keth. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>אהנייא ליה שׁוֹטִיתֵיה וכ׳</he> the myrtle branch (with which he used to dance before bridal couples) was in the old man’s favor (that a phenomenon occurred at his funeral), but some said <he>שְׁטוּתֵיה</he> his folly (v. <cite ref="U00195"><he>שְׁבִשְׁתָּא</he></cite>); others said <he>שיטתיה</he>, v. <cite ref="U00888"><he>שִׁיטְּתָא</he></cite>.
Sabb. 77ᵇ ש׳ שטותא the myrtle branch used at weddings is called shoṭitha as being sh’ṭutha (folly).
